info.title: Elze Backend API
info.description:
REST API of the Elze Node.js backend: authentication, platform administration, company workspaces, people and groups, roles and permissions, dashboard access, the audit trail, the Metadata Lakehouse (context layer) and the BI dashboard engine.

**Responses.** Every JSON response uses one envelope. Success: `{ "success": true, "data": ... }`. Failure: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "...", "details": ... } }`. The `code` is stable and meant for programs; the `message` is meant for people. 5xx messages are generic unless the code is one the API chooses to disclose.

**Signing in.** `POST /api/auth/login` sets three cookies: `da_access` (short-lived access token, HTTP-only, sent on every request), `da_refresh` (long-lived refresh token, HTTP-only, only sent to `/api/auth`) and `da_csrf` (readable by the web app). There is no bearer header.

**CSRF.** Every request that changes something (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) on a signed-in route must send the `x-csrf-token` header with the value of the `da_csrf` cookie.

**Permissions.** Each operation lists the permission it requires in `x-permissions`. A company account holds a permission through its role, limited by the features switched on for its company; the platform owner holds every permission. `x-platform-only` marks routes only the platform owner can call.

**Lists.** Paged lists accept `page`, `pageSize` (at most 100), `search`, `sort` and `dir`, and return the items with the total count.

get.description: Reports whether the access-control catalogue (RBAC bootstrap) has loaded and which email transport is configured. No authentication. Note: the handler sets 503 while starting, but the shared `ok()` response helper resets the status to 200, so the endpoint always answers HTTP 200; read `data.status` (`ok` or `starting`) to tell readiness.

post.description: Signs in with a username or email address and a password, and starts a new session (a new refresh-token family). On success it sets the session cookies: `da_access` (HttpOnly access JWT, path `/`), `da_refresh` (HttpOnly refresh token, path `/api/auth`) and `da_csrf` (non-HttpOnly CSRF token, path `/`; echo its value in the `X-CSRF-Token` header on state-changing requests). `data.state` is `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` when the account must change its password before using the rest of the API. Errors: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (missing identifier or password), 401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` or `COMPANY_DISABLED`, 429 `RATE_LIMITED` (too many failed attempts for this identifier; locked for LOGIN_LOCKOUT_SECONDS), 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. No CSRF token is needed.

Set-Cookie.description: Session cookies: `da_access` (HttpOnly, path `/`, lifetime ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS), `da_refresh` (HttpOnly, path `/api/auth`, lives until the refresh token expires) and `da_csrf` (readable by scripts, path `/`, same lifetime as the refresh token). A legacy `da_access` cookie at path `/api` is cleared.

post.description: Exchanges the `da_refresh` cookie (path `/api/auth`) for a new access token and a rotated refresh token in the same family; the family keeps its original expiry. No request body. Requires the CSRF double-submit: the `X-CSRF-Token` header must equal the `da_csrf` cookie (403 `CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`). On success it sets the session cookies: `da_access` (HttpOnly access JWT, path `/`), `da_refresh` (HttpOnly refresh token, path `/api/auth`) and `da_csrf` (non-HttpOnly CSRF token, path `/`; echo its value in the `X-CSRF-Token` header on state-changing requests). Fails with 401 `INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN` when the cookie is missing, unknown, expired or already used (reuse revokes the whole family), or when the account is disabled or its company inactive; in those cases the session cookies are cleared. 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the catalogue is not loaded.

Set-Cookie.description: Session cookies: `da_access` (HttpOnly, path `/`, lifetime ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS), `da_refresh` (HttpOnly, path `/api/auth`, lives until the refresh token expires) and `da_csrf` (readable by scripts, path `/`, same lifetime as the refresh token). A legacy `da_access` cookie at path `/api` is cleared.

post.description: Revokes the refresh-token family named by the `da_refresh` cookie (if present and valid; problems with it are ignored) and clears the `da_access`, `da_refresh` and `da_csrf` cookies. No request body. Requires the CSRF double-submit (`X-CSRF-Token` header equal to the `da_csrf` cookie), otherwise 403 `CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`. 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the catalogue is not loaded.

get.description: Returns the signed-in account with its effective permission keys, usable feature keys and the dashboards it can open. Works while a password change is pending (then `state` is `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` and `dashboards` is empty). Platform accounts see every dashboard as `admin`; company accounts see dashboards assigned to their company on which they hold a grant (all assigned dashboards as `admin` when they hold `access.grant`). Requires the `da_access` session cookie. Fails with 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`TOKEN_EXPIRED`, or 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `ACCOUNT_PENDING_ACTIVATION` or `COMPANY_DISABLED` when the account or its company is no longer usable; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the access-control catalogue is not loaded.

Lists the signed-in account's active sessions (unrevoked, unexpired refresh-token families), newest first. `current` marks the session the request was made with. Works while a password change is pending. Requires the `da_access` session cookie. Fails with 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`TOKEN_EXPIRED`, or 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `ACCOUNT_PENDING_ACTIVATION` or `COMPANY_DISABLED` when the account or its company is no longer usable; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the access-control catalogue is not loaded.

post.description: Changes the signed-in account's password, clears any must-change-password flag, revokes every existing session of the account and starts a new one. On success it sets the session cookies: `da_access` (HttpOnly access JWT, path `/`), `da_refresh` (HttpOnly refresh token, path `/api/auth`) and `da_csrf` (non-HttpOnly CSRF token, path `/`; echo its value in the `X-CSRF-Token` header on state-changing requests). Allowed while a password change is pending. Errors: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (password policy: at least MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH characters (default 8), at most 200, with at least one digit or symbol; must differ from the current password), 401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` when `currentPassword` is wrong. Requires the `da_access` session cookie. Fails with 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`TOKEN_EXPIRED`, or 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `ACCOUNT_PENDING_ACTIVATION` or `COMPANY_DISABLED` when the account or its company is no longer usable; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the access-control catalogue is not loaded. State-changing request: the `X-CSRF-Token` header must equal the `da_csrf` cookie, otherwise 403 `CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`.

post.description: Consumes an activation token, sets the account's first password, marks the account active, revokes any earlier sessions and signs the user in. Errors: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (token missing or over 200 characters; password policy: at least MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH characters (default 8), at most 200, with at least one digit or symbol), 400 `INVALID_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` (unknown, used or expired), 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` or `COMPANY_DISABLED`, 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.

get.description: Platform-wide counts for the platform console: companies, company accounts, company admins, groups, dashboard assignments, dashboards, and context facts generated/pending across the contexts the caller can see (the fact counts are null if they could not be computed). Platform administrators only: company accounts get 403 `TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED`. Requires the `company.read` permission (403 `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION`, or `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` when the permission belongs to a feature the company does not have). Requires the `da_access` session cookie. Fails with 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`TOKEN_EXPIRED`, or 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `ACCOUNT_PENDING_ACTIVATION` or `COMPANY_DISABLED` when the account or its company is no longer usable; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the access-control catalogue is not loaded. Also fails with 403 `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` while the account must change its password.

post.description: Onboards a company together with its first COMPANY_ADMIN account: creates the company, sets its features (all switchable features when `featureIds` is omitted; locked features are always on), seeds its built-in roles, creates the admin account in the pending state and emails it an activation link. If the email cannot be sent the company is removed again and 502 `EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED` is returned. Errors: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (missing admin object, name 2-150 characters, slug format, username/email rules, unknown feature ids with `details.featureIds`), 409 `CONFLICT` (company name/slug or admin username/email already taken). Platform administrators only: company accounts get 403 `TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED`. Requires the `company.create` permission (403 `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION`, or `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` when the permission belongs to a feature the company does not have). Requires the `da_access` session cookie. Fails with 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`TOKEN_EXPIRED`, or 403 `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `ACCOUNT_PENDING_ACTIVATION` or `COMPANY_DISABLED` when the account or its company is no longer usable; 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the access-control catalogue is not loaded.
